subject.title: [Feature]: this.hasIndexedContent() seems to be called too frequently, causing performance issus

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the existing cache PR now, or require live performance proof before reopening a fix lane?
rationale: The source problem is real, but the repo has a no-new-fix-pr label and the only open closing PR is unmergeable and not maintainer-modifiable, so automation should not create another branch without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt or replace the cache fix
options.body: Allow a maintainer-owned or maintainer-modifiable PR that preserves the narrow cache approach, adds invalidation and query-count proof, and supersedes the conflicting external PR.

options.title: Wait for benchmark proof
options.body: Keep this issue open but require a live benchmark or query-count reproduction before spending more review time on the optimization.

options.title: Decline the optimization
options.body: Close the issue as accepted performance debt if maintainers prefer the direct SQLite probe for correctness simplicity.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace the cache fix
recommendation.body: Allow a maintainer-owned or maintainer-modifiable PR that preserves the narrow cache approach, adds invalidation and query-count proof, and supersedes the conflicting external PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The preflight helper and bundled memory-plugin boundary history make this the best available routing signal for the cache-shape decision.
